Object.freeze is shallow. It prevents mutation of the object's own properties, not nested objects. So `cfg.db` stays mutable even though `cfg` is frozen. Trying to reassign `cfg.db` would fail, but mutating its contents (`cfg.db.host = 'y'`) works.

I was wrong. Object.freeze does not freeze "everything reachable from it"—only the immediate object. To lock down nested structures, you need recursive freezing (or a library like `immer` or `structuralySharedClone`).
